For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the apple juice came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-apple-juice" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-apple-juice-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of apple juice, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Apple juice FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-apple-juice" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-apple-juice" data-question="What heavy metals are found in apple juice?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in apple juice?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, AsIII, AsV, Cr(III) and CrVI in apple juice, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anastácio M, Marreilha dos Santos AP, Aschner M, Mateus L · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Determination of trace metals in fruit juices in the Portuguese market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 434-439</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in apple juice, juice from 350 results in 4 reporting regions, with a subgroup median of 18 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-apple-juice-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-apple-juice-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of apple juice measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of apple juice measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 333 groups of apple juice ranged from 0.1 µg/kg (FY2011) to 67 µg/kg (FY2014); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018">Analytical Results for Lead in Juice Sampled Under the FDA&#39;s Toxic Elements in Food and Foodware, and Radionuclides in Food – Import and Domestic Compliance Program (FY2005-FY2018)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 7 groups of apple juice ranged from 2 µg/kg (imported nectar, producer code N (sample 23)) to 6 µg/kg (imported nectar, producer code E (sample 20)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-apple-juice-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-apple-juice-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in apple juice is inorganic?">
